findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization branch renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: In tableResultComponent, when the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature flag is enabled, the code renders <TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} /> instead of the actual table results. The new component is never wired to `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, `fieldAliases`, or the loading state, so any organization with the flag enabled will see a completely blank table widget in dashboards (real query results are discarded). The real data mapping only exists in the non-flagged StyledSimpleTableChart path. Either pass the actual data/columns to TableWidgetVisualization or don't ship the flag branch until it's wired up.

findings.title: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration
findings.body: In this diff, `_truncate_title` is added as a staticmethod on `CommitContextIntegration`, but `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` invokes it as `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`. PRCommentWorkflow is the workflow class used by the GitHub/GitLab integrations and is not a subclass of CommitContextIntegration, so this lookup raises AttributeError at runtime whenever a merged-PR comment is generated, breaking PR comment posting for GitHub and GitLab. The call should reference `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title` (or be inlined).

findings.title: fetch_error_details zips error_ids against events.values(), mispairing IDs with data
findings.body: fetch_error_details builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, fetches them via `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then pairs results with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id containing only the nodes that were found (and not necessarily in the input order). If any node is missing, or the dict iteration order differs from the input order, each error_id gets paired with the wrong event's data, producing incorrect titles/messages and attributing errors to the wrong event IDs in the Seer summary. It should iterate over the node_id->data mapping (e.g. zip(node_ids, ...) with lookups per id, or `events.get(node_id)`) so IDs and payloads stay aligned.

findings.title: Nodestore event timestamps are strings but are compared against numeric breadcrumb timestamps
findings.body: fetch_error_details reads `timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` straight from the nodestore payload, where event timestamps are stored as ISO-8601 strings (not numbers). gen_request_data then compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`, i.e. str < float, which raises TypeError in Python 3 as soon as there is at least one error event and one breadcrumb event, turning the summarize endpoint into a 500. The nodestore timestamp needs to be parsed to a numeric epoch value (and note the default of 0.0 is also inconsistent with the string type) before sorting/interleaving.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only filtered out while a search query is active
findings.body: The new HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES list ('is_segment', 'project_id', 'received') is only applied inside the branch that runs when `searchQuery.trim()` is non-empty; when the search box is empty the code returns `sorted` unfiltered. That means these internal attributes are visible in the default span-attributes view but disappear as soon as the user types anything, which is inconsistent and almost certainly not the intent of a constant named HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES. The filter should be applied to the sorted list regardless of whether a search query is present.

findings.title: Shipped migrations 0917/0920 replaced with no-ops and their test deleted; conversion now depends entirely on 0921
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 convert_org_saved_searches_to_views migrations are gutted to `return` with a comment pointing at 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, and the migration test for 0917 is deleted. These migrations are marked is_post_deployment and dated months ago, so some environments (self-hosted installs, staging) may have already recorded them as applied; more importantly, if migration 0921 is not present in this branch's migration chain, organization-level saved searches will silently never be converted to group search views and the data migration coverage is gone. This should be verified (and ideally kept as an explicit no-op with a linked ticket) before merging.

findings.title: Feedback summary endpoint (backed by an LLM call) is fetched on every feedback list page view with only a 5s staleTime
findings.body: useFeedbackSummary fires a request to /organizations/<slug>/feedback-summary/ whenever the feedback list mounts for orgs with 'user-feedback-ai-summaries', with staleTime of only 5 seconds and no other caching or debouncing. The backend usecase (generate_summary) performs an LLM completion, so navigating to or refreshing the feedback list can trigger a new LLM generation per visit per user, which is both slow (the UI shows a placeholder) and expensive. Consider a much longer staleTime/cache, or generating the summary server-side with caching keyed on the query/window.

findings.title: Tests no longer exercise the application/reports+json custom parser
findings.body: The rewritten tests post all reports with the default JSON content type; the previous versions used content_type="application/reports+json" to cover BrowserReportsJSONParser, which is the media type real browsers use for the Reporting API. Since the endpoint's parser_classes list is the only thing making that content type work, a regression there (e.g. parser removed or media_type typo) would no longer be caught. Add at least one test that posts with the reports+json content type.
